programme: NR1H2 (LXRβ) sits at the top of a macrophage cholesterol-handling/nuclear-receptor module (targets CETP, SCARB1, ABCA1, ABCG1, APOE, PLTP — the reverse-cholesterol-transport and cholesterol-efflux machinery), paired with ESRRA (ERRα) driving the linked oxidative/mitochondrial metabolic arm (PPARA, PPARGC1A, ACADM, CYC1, CYCS) that nuclear-receptor crosstalk literature ties to LXR signaling in lipid-laden macrophages. AEBP1 feeds the same cell with lipid-uptake and foam-cell targets (CD36, FABP4, APOE, TNF), while HBP1 sits downstream as a repressor of the inflammatory and proliferative output of that same macrophage/vascular-cell state (TNF, IL1B, MPO, TLR2, CD74, plus the RB1/CDKN2A cell-cycle arm governing plaque-cell proliferation). Together this is the transcriptional core of macrophage foam-cell formation and plaque inflammation — i.e., an atherogenesis programme, not a generic immune or developmental signature.
role_in_a: In Cardiovascular_Disease this programme is the engine of atherosclerotic plaque biology: LXRβ/NR1H2-driven cholesterol efflux (ABCA1/ABCG1/APOE) opposing AEBP1/CD36/FABP4-driven lipid uptake sets net foam-cell lipid load, with HBP1 modulating the resulting TNF/IL1B/MPO inflammatory output and smooth-muscle/macrophage proliferation that determines plaque growth and instability.
role_in_b: In Stroke — specifically the large-vessel/atherothrombotic subtype — the same circulating monocyte/macrophage programme operating in the carotid and cerebral vessel wall is expected to govern plaque burden and rupture risk upstream of the ischemic event, and the same myeloid inflammatory output (MPO, TNF, IL1B) is consistent with the systemic and post-ischemic inflammatory state seen in stroke blood.
shared_axis: Ischemic stroke is mechanistically downstream of arterial atherosclerosis in a large fraction of cases, so a blood-derived monocyte/macrophage lipid-handling and inflammatory-repressor module built around LXRβ, ERRα, AEBP1 and HBP1 would be expected to recur across cohorts of both diseases simply because both are reading out the same underlying atherosclerotic process in circulating myeloid cells, not because the diseases are otherwise related.
reasoning: NR1H2/LXR is a canonical, textbook node of macrophage cholesterol efflux and atherogenesis, and AEBP1/HBP1's target sets (CD36, FABP4, TNF, IL1B, MPO) are recognizable foam-cell/inflammatory genes, so the module is nameable and biologically coherent for both diseases separately. But the retrieved record never states the CVD–Stroke connection directly — Open Targets shows no CVD association for any of the four factors (partly a query-naming artifact) and the stroke-labeled papers for NR1H2 discuss adipose tissue and aneurysm models rather than stroke proper, so the CVD-to-stroke bridge rests on general atherosclerosis biology rather than anything retrieved here.
support: PMID 33788111 — shows LXRβ (NR1H2), alongside PPARγ, expressed in adipose depots in a cardiometabolic context, consistent with a lipid-handling nuclear-receptor role but not stroke-specific; PMID 27021877 — shows a macrophage-dependent vascular pathology (aneurysm formation) modulated by metabolic/hyperglycemic state, indirectly consistent with macrophage lipid/inflammatory involvement of NR1H2 but not disease-matched to clinical stroke. No usable PMID was given for AEBP1, ESRRA, or HBP1's disease-relevant papers (their further hits were unjudged/unnumbered in the record), so their placement rests on target-gene identity alone.
how_to_falsify: In monocytes/macrophages isolated from matched CVD and atherothrombotic-stroke patients versus controls, check whether NR1H2 target genes (ABCA1, ABCG1, SCARB1, CETP) move concordantly with AEBP1 targets (CD36, FABP4) and HBP1 targets (TNF, IL1B, MPO) across both diseases; then perturb NR1H2 (LXR agonist/antagonist) ex vivo and test whether AEBP1 and HBP1 target expression shifts in the predicted opposing/repressive direction. If the three factors' target programs vary independently of each other, or if disease status doesn't track with coordinated shifts in this gene set, the proposed shared macrophage module is not the right explanation for the recurrence.
caveats: Both diseases were profiled in the same tissue (blood), so overlap may partly reflect shared circulating-cell composition rather than disease-specific biology. Only 4 independent cohort pairs underlie the 24 patient-group comparisons, so the counts (16/24 for NR1H2, 12/24 for the other three) have limited independent replication. Open Targets returned no formal Cardiovascular_Disease association for any factor here, flagged in the record as likely a non-standard disease-name query artifact rather than true absence — this should not be read as evidence against the module. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed several canonical vascular/immune master regulators (KLF2, TAL1, ERG, STAT1, IRF1, CEBPB, LEF1), and the single-view exclusions removed a cluster of interferon-response factors (IRF5/6/9) that did not generalize — both are consistent with this account, which deliberately does not lean on tissue-generic or interferon-driven stories. TLE5, ZNF143, SOX4, HOXB3, HSF2, BCL11B, ISL1 and TCF3 also recurred but do not fit this lipid/macrophage programme and are not treated as part of it.
